items.summary: An MCP server that puts every coding agent on one machine (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Gemini CLI and more) on a single bus: see who is running, tag agents by project, model or PR, and message one agent, a selector group, or everyone at once; an urgent message can wake an idle agent mid-session. Messages are clearly marked as coming from a peer agent and can never approve actions. One npx command installs it and everything stays local; cross-machine messaging and remote control over Tailscale are on the roadmap, not yet shipped.
items.title: pulsar: A message bus for coding agents across harnesses — agents message each other and wake idle sessions (Show HN Nov 17, MIT)

items.summary: An open-source Electron desktop app from a Checkly engineer: each project gets its own area on a zoomable map, and agent sessions, tickets, PRs, reviews and rollouts are items on it. Agents are plain Claude Code or Codex sessions that read and write the map through an MCP server, and a 'Needs me' panel collects only the items waiting on you. Data stays in local SQLite; the author says it doubled the PRs he merges each week.
items.title: Agentic Crafting Table: Manage a dozen parallel agent sessions, tickets and PRs on one zoomable map (Show HN Nov 17, open source)

items.summary: OpenStatus' open-source AI SRE agent, hosted by you: when an alert fires it gathers context, proposes a concrete mitigation — rollback, restart or scale up — within a few tool calls, then investigates the root cause and posts both to Slack. Read-only by default and never acts on its own; the one opt-in exception is Fly.io machine actions, which run only after a named human approves. Claude by default, with OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama and more supported; logs and metrics are queried on demand, nothing is ingested.
items.title: Stromboli: A self-hosted AI SRE agent that stops the bleeding when an alert fires, then reports the root cause to Slack (Show HN Nov 16, MIT)
